articleTitle: In the beginning (of the British Calibration Service)
publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: This is a personal recollection of why and how the British Calibration Service (BCS) came into being. Historians remind us that by looking backwards we should see more clearly the way ahead. As a founder-member of BCS, the authors aims this article to serve as a pointer for future endeavours.

publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: The global market for sales of electronic test and measurement equipment has increased in size considerably over the past 30 years and is estimated at 9000 million (US) dollars. Meanwhile, the maintenance costs industry about $2000M of which $1200M is for provision of calibration services; a market that has developed almost entirely during this period. In many world-wide markets, certification against ISO9000 has become an initial requirement of prospective suppliers. In the UK alone, 45 thousand entities have such registration in 1996 and, for some, regular calibration of their measuring equipment is a new practice driven by the standard. Yet many instrument users are unfamiliar with the intricacies of calibration and concentrate upon their core competency. Consequently, they look to other companies offering the specialist skills and resources necessary; vendors that are independently assessed against ISO9000 or, less likely, against technical competency criteria based on ISO/IEC Guide 25 (or European Norm EN45001) such as UKAS accreditation. The author discusses these developments and looks into the likely future trends in this field.

articleTitle: The role of INTA's international accreditation in supporting Spanish industrial metrology: past, present and future
publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: The need for an accredited metrological infrastructure arose in the Institute towards the end of the Sixties, due to its activities in the international forum, and in particular to those of a contractual nature requiring continuous audits. Since 1972, the year in which INTA obtained the accreditation of the British Calibration Service (BCS) (now UKAS), up to the current metrological situation, the role of INTA in supporting Spanish industrial metrology has evolved considerably. The UKAS accreditation enabled INTA to support those national industries who set up quality assurance systems, mainly in the aeronautical, energy and petrochemical sectors. The Institute also acted as the Reference Laboratory for the Industrial Calibration System (SCI) in five of the ten measurement areas accredited. The contribution of the Institute's Area of Metrology and Calibration to industry is described from a historical point of view, defining its present situation with respect to the national metrological infrastructure and the future possibilities.

articleTitle: Supervision of measuring equipment by accredited laboratories: a quality system element
publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: Modern industrial production is characterized by an increasing complexity of products and manufacturing procedures and, in addition, by an international division of labour. This has led to the development of quality management systems with the aim of avoiding faulty products and faults in the production at each stage, from the design to the delivery of a product. A certified quality management system according to ISO 9000 strengthens the position of a company on the national and international markets and guarantees the purchaser that the products of a company have been manufactured in compliance with the company's quality policy. One important element of a quality system is the handling of measuring, test and inspection equipment which is used in production and for quality control. This element is also an indispensable part of all ISO 9000 standards. The regular calibration of measuring instruments and the supervision of measuring equipment are necessary prerequisites for reliable measurements and therefore strongly influence product quality. This close interdependence between metrology and quality management is reflected in the ISO 9000 series which requires that the measuring equipment is calibrated in a way that ensures traceability to national standards of measurement. The main reasons for the establishment of "Deutscher Kalibrierdienst"-the German national accreditation body for calibration laboratories, are outlined and international co-operation in calibration and testing are discussed.

articleTitle: SPC in calibration: the good, the bad and the ugly!
publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: Electronic measuring instruments are often involved in the collection of data relating to a production process. This data is utilised to monitor the process in order to understand it better and the parameters are usually described statistically. With this statistical knowledge the process can be refined and adjusted in some way to improve its output, for example a product, in terms of quality and/or cost. In effect this is a stochastic feedback loop around the process and called SPC - Statistical Process Control. The author discusses the use of the SPC technique in instrument calibration and production process control.

publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: Calibration is an integral part of any reliable process measurement, irrespective of whether the process is chemical, manufacturing or testing. The type of measuring equipment in use, the working environment and the operating system must also be considered in order to achieve the overall process requirement.

publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: Calibration plays an important part of today's manufacturing process, and close control is placed by the UKAS upon the measuring techniques employed by those who provide calibration services. But what controls are there covering the actual process of calibration? In a quality-driven manufacturing process, knowledge of the performance of a piece of test equipment yesterday (i.e. before it was sent for calibration) is just as important as its performance today. Having accurate, believable calibration data concerning the performance of that equipment as it was last used is every bit as important as the final calibration report.

articleTitle: A generic DMM test and calibration strategy
publicationTitle: Contribution of Instrument Calibration to Product Quality
abstract: The digital multimeter (DMM) is one of the most widely used electrical measurement instruments and provides electrical traceability to many industrial users. However, it is the nature of measurement products that they require regular checks to ensure that they operate not only in a functional sense, but also within their specifications. Such regular checks are known as calibrations and require a certain amount of knowledge of DMM technology in order to calibrate them effectively. This paper seeks to identify the important functional and calibration parameters and to offer a generic guidance strategy for their routine verification.
